prior art: pad-share band (ideal 0.75-1.7x, ok 0.2-4x of min(3.5% width, 3.5em)) -> comfortable padding roughly 2.6-6% of a narrow box's own width, capped ~3.5em (56px at 16px) once the box is wide. frame-gap (gap/font-size at nearest text): ideal 0.45-2.2, cramped<0.35, touching<0.12. log.msg: measured: framed-box padding as %-of-own-width -> p10=0.6%, p25=1.7%, median=5.8%, p75=13.3%, p90=26%, max=120% (a few full-bleed outliers). padEm p10=0.4em median=1.0em p90=1.4em. Zero real-content box (w>=150px, text>=15 chars) exceeded 20% of its own width -- confirms owner's '30% almost always too much' ceiling is essentially never crossed here; risk is entirely on the cramped side.

chased ~10 apparent 0-padding text boxes with playwright to check for real crampedness (alignment-vs-padding.md's own warning): most were false alarms -- sidebar/rail (child .sidebar-link owns 0.64em/1.4em padding), page-preview-thumb (child has .pad), panel-workspace clock (0 padding but content is centered, never reaches the edge), imagine-item chip row (children own the pad), md-details (border-top is a SEPARATOR not an enclosing frame -- my hasBorder<=0.5px check treated a hairline rule as a box). Genuine finding: the framed-box detector over-fires on border-top-only dividers; a real frame check needs >=2 opposite sides.

closest real near-misses (comfortable but zero margin): house `code{padding:0.15em 0.4em}` and pill-style chips (scene-hint 0.9px/0.1em vertical) sit right at the 0.35em cramped threshold -- fine as shot, no slack if font-size or line-height shifts.
